sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know *quisiera* from B2 Unit 9, together with *pudiera* and *debiera*. They are the *-ra* forms of *querer*, *poder* and *deber*, and they soften a request or a piece of advice in the same way as *querría*, *podría* and *debería*. Only the *-ra* form works like this: *quisiese* does not soften a request. You also know *agradecería* from B2 Unit 9, which is followed by *que* and the imperfect subjunctive (*Le agradecería que me enviara el contrato*).

sections.title: One more pattern: quisiera que
sections.content: *Quisiera* can also be followed by *que* and the imperfect subjunctive, when you want someone else to do something: *Quisiera que me explicara el trámite* "I would like you to explain the procedure to me". You know *Quiero que comas* from B2 Unit 4: with one subject use the infinitive (*Quisiera hablar con usted*), and with two subjects use *que* + subjunctive. The verb after *quisiera que* is in the imperfect subjunctive, which keeps the same distance and politeness as *quisiera* itself. Compare the direct *Quiero que me ayude* with the softer *Quisiera que me ayudara*.

sections.title: Polite forms
rows: I would like to speak to the director.
Could you tell me where the office is?
You ought to rest a little.
Quisiera que me explicara cómo funciona.
I would like you to explain how it works.
We would like you to see us tomorrow.

items.spanish: Buenos días, quisiera que me ayudara con este documento.
items.english: Good morning, I would like you to help me with this document.
Could you wait a moment, please?

items.spanish: Debiéramos revisar el contrato antes de firmarlo.
items.english: We ought to check the contract before signing it.

sections.content: Keep the *-ra* form in all of these: *quisiera*, never *quisiese*, to ask for something politely. After *quisiera que*, do not use the indicative or the conditional: *Quisiera que me ayudara*, not *Quisiera que me ayudo* or *Quisiera que me ayudaría*.
